extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting speculative fiction to Strange Horizons (prospective magazine contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting short speculative fiction to the Strange Horizons magazine, including eligibility, formatting, rights, payment, and editorial preferences. Intended to help authors prepare and transmit stories that fit the magazine's requirements and tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission window / timing
rubrics_metrics.description: We are open to fiction submissions between Monday 1600 UTC and Tuesday 1600 UTC, every week of the year except during the month of December.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the top of the page to confirm we are open before submitting. The page links to current UTC time for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative-fiction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We want: Speculative fiction, broadly defined. If your story doesn't have a speculative element, or strong speculative-fiction sensibilities, it's probably not for us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All subgenres and forms of speculative fiction are welcome, but stories should demonstrate speculative sensibility rather than being essentially non-speculative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count limits and preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 10,000 words (under 5000 preferred). We prefer stories under 5,000 words, but consider stories up to 10,000 words. We have no minimum wordcount requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The longer the story, the less likely we are to be interested. The wordcount limit is not absolutely inflexible, but we can't consider stories much over the limit, not even as serials. Story length is determined by word-processor wordcount rounded up to the next highest 100 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats and manuscript formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send only RTF, DOC or DOCX files and try to stick to standard manuscript format as much as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use typical manuscript conventions where feasible; nonstandard formats may complicate consideration. If your story is nontraditional (hypertext, interactive), query first to discuss submission logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (Moksha system only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted through our Moksha submissions system — no email or postal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We can only track and consider stories submitted through that form. If you have trouble submitting, e-mail fiction@strangehorizons.com with 'QUERY:' at the beginning of the subject line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous and multiple submissions / resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous or multiple submissions; no re-submissions. Please wait 7 days after receiving a rejection before you submit again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the same story to other venues simultaneously. Do not submit multiple stories at once from the same author. Stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons (even revised) will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously unpublished in English / rights purchased
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously unpublished in English — we buy first English rights, including audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We buy first-printing world exclusive English-language rights for six (6) months. After that period you are free to republish the story elsewhere. We hope to leave the story in our archives indefinitely, but you may remove it from the archives at any time after one (1) year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special note on translations and Samovar
rubrics_metrics.description: Our quarterly sister magazine Samovar specializes in translations and offers a better pay rate of 12¢/word USD split between author and translator; translations submitted to either magazine will always be considered for both: first for Samovar and second for Strange Horizons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We encourage translations to be submitted directly to Samovar. If you don't want your translation forwarded to Samovar, state this in your cover letter and we will consider it only for Strange Horizons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rate and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay 8¢/word USD, with a minimum payment of $60. Payment is made within 60 days of contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SFWA officially considers Strange Horizons a professional market. Payment is made by check or PayPal per the author's preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial preferences — themes and styles we like
rubrics_metrics.description: Some particular things we love, or are interested in: Fiction from or about diverse perspectives and traditionally under-represented groups, written from a non-exoticizing and well-researched position; unusual yet readable styles and inventive structures and narratives; stories that address political issues in complex and nuanced ways, resisting oversimplification; hypertext fiction, interactive fiction, and other stories that explore and exploit the forms available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have hypertext/interactive work you think might fit, please query to discuss how to submit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content allowances and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Profanity is fine. Sex or violence in a story should be artistically justified; no excessive gore. We welcome submissions from anywhere in the world, and British spellings are fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whatever words are appropriate for your story, but avoid gratuitous/excessive gore. Cultural and regional spelling variants are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of works previously published in another language
rubrics_metrics.description: We will consider stories which have previously appeared in another language, but have never been published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such translations are eligible; see the Samovar policy if the submission is a translation and consider submitting directly to Samovar for better pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable submissions / exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Things we won't consider: Stories above 10,000 words, including serialized novels or novellas; partial or incomplete stories; unsolicited reprints of works previously published in English; stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons (even if revised); multiple stories at once from the same author; submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously; poetry or nonfiction (we are the wrong department for those).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please don't send part of a story and ask us to request the rest. Ensure the work is complete, within length, and not previously published in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your cover letter can be minimal: generally, these should be short and list just a few of your most recent or most relevant publications or workshops. If you've got life experience relevant to your story, please do mention that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letters shouldn't include plot synopses or pitches. If in doubt, consult the sample cover letters page linked on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autoresponder and contact procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: We send an autoresponder message in response to every submission we receive. If you haven't received an autoresponse within 24 hours after submitting, please query immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing an autoresponse usually means we have an incorrect email address for you and won't be able to contact you when we make a decision on your fiction. Use subject line 'QUERY: Your Question Topic' when emailing fiction@strangehorizons.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response times and patience policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We usually respond within a few weeks, but are currently running behind and response times are slower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please query if you're concerned your submission has gone astray, but otherwise be patient with us while we catch up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit a story, we strongly prefer you don't withdraw it. If you withdraw a story, we won't consider any version of that story in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do need to withdraw a story, please send an e-mail telling us that you need to withdraw and let us know why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordcount measurement and rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: We determine story length by taking the word-processor wordcount and rounding up to the next highest 100 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check their word-processor counts and be aware that the magazine rounds up, which may affect whether a submission exceeds the preferred limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archives and post-publication rights
rubrics_metrics.description: We hope you'll allow us to leave the story in our archives indefinitely after it's rotated off the main table of contents, but you have the right to remove your story from the archives at any time after one (1) year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial rights purchase is a six-month first-printing world exclusive English-language right; after six months you regain broader republication rights.
